llm_notes.aerogarden bounty vs harvest:
- **Noise:** The **Harvest** is generally quiet, but several reviews note the **Bounty** is *at least as quiet and sometimes quieter*; both make a low pump hum that is usually fine for a kitchen or living room, but can be noticeable in a very quiet bedroom.[1][3][6][10][18]
- **Cost:** The **Harvest** is the cheaper entry model at about **$80–120** or **$109.95**, while the **Bounty** is about **$230** or **$229.95**; the Bounty also tends to cost more to run and buy accessories for because it is the larger 9-pod system.[13][15][6]
- **Apartment fit:** **Harvest** fits tighter spaces better because it is smaller and lower-height, while **Bounty** fits well if you have more counter space and want 9 pods or taller plants; Bounty is better for a kitchen counter, Harvest is better for compact apartment setups.[3][15][18]
llm_notes.aerogarden farm vs farm plus:
- **Noise:** Both the **Farm** and **Farm Plus** use a small water pump that produces a **soft hum/trickling sound** on a cycle; it is usually not disruptive, but it is **audible in quiet rooms**.[2][6][20]
- **Cost:** The **Farm 24 Plus** is listed at **$599.95 MSRP** in one comparison, and the **Farm 24 / Farm** line is estimated at about **$96.40/year** to run for electricity, with the 24-pod version costing roughly **about twice** the 12-pod unit.[4][19]
- **Apartment fit:** The **Farm Plus** is the better apartment fit of the two if you need more vertical room: it offers **24" grow height** and is about **34" x 36" x 14"**, while the **XL/Farm larger-height versions** take more space; the Farm line is a **floor-standing** unit, so it is better for apartments with dedicated floor space than for tight studio layouts.[1][17][18]
llm_notes.aerogarden trellis for 2019 bounty model:
- **Noise:** The Bounty’s pump is designed to be quiet; AeroGarden says most sound is **water noise** from the pump and dripping tray, though some users report **gurgling**. [15][9]
- **Cost:** The **AeroGarden Trellis for 2019 Bounty Models** is listed at **$14.36** on AeroGarden accessories, and **$17.95** on ScottsMiracle-Gro pages. [7][3][13]
- **Apartment fit:** It fits **2019 or newer Bounty family** gardens and **adds 12 inches of support** for taller plants; it **does not fit Harvest** models, so it is a good apartment option only if you already have a compatible Bounty unit. [1][15]
